source: EPA version 11.1.docx, page 8 — 'Workplace-based assessment (WBA) tools' and 'Standard assessment information sources'

answers.D2: NO — page 8 does not specify the instruments. It defines the TOOLS (nine, one sentence each) and then, separately, the four INFORMATION SOURCES that ground every summative decision. Neither is a form specification: no field sets, no per-tool rating scale, no required/optional structure. The form designs still have to be asked for.
answers.D3: CCA = 'Clinical Case Analysis'. The reconciling reading is correct: its definition is documentation review AND discussion of the reasoning, in one instrument.
answers.D5: RCA = 'Random Case Analysis'. Confirms the recommendation verbatim.

wba_tools_defined_on_page_8.definition: Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise — direct observation of a focused clinical encounter, followed by immediate feedback.
Direct Observation of Procedural Skills — observation of a trainee performing a procedure, assessing technique, patient interaction and safety.
Case-Based Discussion — a structured discussion of a case the trainee has managed, exploring clinical reasoning and decision-making.
Clinical Case Analysis — review of clinical documentation and discussion of the reasoning and management plan recorded.
Random Case Analysis — review of cases selected at random from the trainee's records to identify knowledge gaps.
Multi-Source Feedback — structured feedback from colleagues across the multidisciplinary team and, where appropriate, from patients' families.
Observation of the trainee in routine clinical practice, including ward rounds, handover and family meetings.
A cycle of measurement against an agreed standard, followed by change and re-measurement.
A written or verbal reflection on a challenging case or critical incident, discussed with a supervisor or mentor.

standard_assessment_information_sources.preamble: The same set of information sources grounds the summative entrustment decision for every EPA in this document. It is therefore set out once here rather than repeated in each EPA.
sources: Clinical documentation — notes, referrals, discharge summaries and prescriptions.
Colleagues — consultants, registrars, peers and members of the multidisciplinary team, including nursing and allied health staff and support services such as radiology and laboratory services.
Patients, guardians and family members — their experience of the care provided.
The candidate — self-reflection on the milestones achieved, and learning plans that promote progressive milestone achievement.
standard_assessment_information_sources.closing: Each EPA specifies how often the activity should be observed, and who takes the summative entrustment decision.

governance_statement_from_page_4: The summative entrustment decision for an EPA is taken by the Clinical Competency Committee, drawing on the standard assessment information sources set out on page 8 — never by a single assessor and never from a single form.
